The app is so stupid that it doesn’t recognize phone numbers with just a city or region in the caller ID field as being scam calls. There is no way to block all incoming calls that don’t have a proper name in the caller ID field. There is no way to block all incoming international calls (most of the scam calls I’ve seen are from Canadian and Filipino numbers). There is no way to make your phone white list only for incoming calls. This app is about a decade behind the times and is completely ineffectual. I am seriously considering my options in regard to switching phone service providers because of these glaring deficiencies in AT&T Active Armor and AT&T in general.

PS: To whoever the customer service rep is who is tasked with replying with 80% prewritten copy-paste replies: I will NOT email the user experience team or dev team about this, as I have already left my feedback here. Instead of creating extra friction and hurdles for users to go through, why not use some lean principles and simply forward the reviews to the user experience team and/or dev team? Otherwise, what is the point of what you are doing? It’s 2026. Nobody is really fooled by the “acknowledge, repeat user’s words, then move conversation to private channel” template response anymore.

reviews.title: Reporting VPN bug issue
reviews.text:
I've used the AT&T ActiveArmor app since day one, when it first rolled out. For the most part, it’s been great, until recently. 

I’m a career Techie & understand how important it is, especially in this day and age, to protect our lives that, sadly, exist on our phones. That said, the VPN service/option in the ActiveArmor app has been having serious issues for months. 

When I put my phone down for the night, I make sure that I go into app updates. I update every app that needs updating, then go into “Settings” and make sure I’m connected to my personal internet. VPN is set (always set) to ‘ON’, and after checking that, I can put my phone under my pillow for the night so I can get a good night's sleep. 

However, the app’s VPN has had a bug that’s been plaguing my brand-new 17 Pro Max (purchased from the Apple Store on November 9, 2025) for the last 5 to 6 months. 

Issue::
Every night, someone or something causes the ActiveArmor VPN to automatically turn off. I know this because I’ve been monitoring it for the last few months, which is/has been affecting my already diagnosed  ‘Chronic Insomnia’. 

I’m adding some context to this reported bug issue so that you know that I know what I’m talking about. 

I use one VPN, and it’s ActiveArmor. I know that using more than one VPN at the same time can/will cause interference, allowing hackers to access everything on my cell, which nowadays is a person’s entire life. 

Because I rely on the app daily and all it offers, I’m advising y

reviews.title: Destroyed battery life over time
reviews.text:
I liked the idea of the AT&T ActiveArmor app, and for a while it did help reduce spam and unwanted calls. I’ve used it for close to 10 years, so I definitely gave it a fair chance.
Unfortunately, over time the app has become more of a problem than a benefit. It started destroying my battery life, and since uninstalling it, my battery has been noticeably better. Even with the app installed, spam and unwanted calls still made it through, so the protection never felt fully reliable.
At this point, with Apple’s built-in security, call filtering, and privacy features improving so much, ActiveArmor feels outdated and unnecessary. I appreciate what it was meant to do, but the battery drain and inconsistent results made it no longer worth keeping on my phone.

reviews.title: Good from far, however, far from good.
reviews.text: In the beginning this app seemed like it was everything I wanted in mobile protection. For starters it’s not free for me and I’m with AT&T’s FirstNet program. It does come free for those outside of FirstNet if you’re only with AT&T. That’s a bummer but I can get over that. What I can’t get over is the fact that it significantly reduces my internet speed by like 50% and I got an iPhone 17pro. It doesn’t allow me to access my healthcare benefits with the military  and as a result, I’m currently locked out of my account and need to call TRICARE to have them unlock my account. All this because it wouldn’t fully load the page. Yet my iPad that’s also connected with FirstNet and WITHOUT ActiveArmor loads just fine. The message I got was  “To Many Failed Attempts”. I don’t know how when I unlocked it with my FACE!!!! But the app will warn the hell out of you when you disconnect and reconnect to some good WiFi only to slow down the speeds again by like 50%. So it’s a lose lose. Your best bet is delete the app and enjoy that 5G+ without ActiveArmor throttling/reducing your internet speeds and locking you out of much needed access to YOUR accounts.

reviews.title: Prices Increased While Effectiveness Continues to Decline
reviews.text:
The app keeps getting worse instead of improving. It shows that a “Spam Risk” caller was blocked, yet the call still came through and the caller was able to leave a voicemail. If the call was truly blocked, how did it still reach my phone?

It’s difficult to justify the continued price increases when the core functionality doesn’t work as advertised. The whole purpose of this service is to stop spam calls from reaching customers in the first place. Instead, the app logs them as “blocked” after the fact while the calls still get through. 

For a paid service, this is frustrating and misleading. I would expect stronger spam filtering, better accuracy, and actual blocking before the call reaches my phone—not simply labeling it afterward.

reviews.title: Does not block anymore
reviews.text: When I first started using this app, it was great! It blocked all the spam risk calls. I have the setting set to block spam risk calls. In addition to other calls that I have manually designated to be blocked. Now here we are in February 2026 and for the last two months or so none of the spam calls have been blocked. All of them are not only ringing through to my phone, but they are also going to my voicemail. It is kind of pointless because if that’s the case, then I would just use the Block feature on my iPhone. It used to block these calls and they would not be even allowed to ring towards my phone nor would I see the notification that the call came through now suddenly I am seeing the notification as well as them in my voicemail. Please fix this and put it back the way it was.

reviews.title: App defective due to poor programming.

This app is a scam to get you to use ATT. Still after months this app Is defective. It just sends me to the App Store saying it needs an update but the app is fully updated.  App defective due to poor programming. App defective due to poor programming. App defective due to poor programming. Many months later it is still defective. I have the latest operating system available for my phone fully updated but still this app will not work because my phone is not new. This app is a ATT scam.

reviews.title: Showing ads in notification
reviews.text:
I got a notification that is an ad for their service, not a phone call notification. It said “Bank with Confidence Block Suspicious Websites.” You can’t be showing me ads for services without giving me the option to turn off the ad. This is a violation of Apple’s App Review Guidelines 4.5.4 “Push Notifications should not be used for promotions or direct marketing purposes unless customers have explicitly opted in to receive them via consent language displayed in your app’s UI, and you provide a method in your app for a user to opt out from receiving such messages. Abuse of these services may result in revocation of your privileges.” I have reported this to Apple.

Edit: your response is garbage. You say it’s not marketing. The notification is promotion for a paid service. “Push Notifications should not be used for promotions or direct marketing purposes” is not ambiguous.
